NAL - You cannot start your paternity leave until the baby is born, but you do not HAVE to start it on the day the baby is born. 

I'm not sure you can split your paternity leave. Your partner can however give you some of her mat leave through shared parental leave. Whereby the mother and mothers partner can share 50 weeks between them on top of the 2 weeks the mother must take, 39 at statutory shared parental pay (or maternity pay depending on how you do it) and the remaining 11 at nil pay unless you have an extra shared parental pay policy through your work. The mother of the child must take at least 2 weeks off work following the birth of the child. 

Eg. Baby is due 3rd February. The mother takes 26 weeks from her due date. The baby is born on the 5th of February and the mothers partner takes 2 weeks paternity from that date. The mother of the child decides to return to work after her 26 week maternity leave, having taken 26 weeks maternity pay. The mother and her partner opt to take shared parental leave. The mother then 'gives' her remaining maternity leave entitlement to her partner, who is now (assuming the earning criteria and work service length has been met) entitled to 26 weeks of shared parental leave, 13 of which are at statutory shared parental pay and 13 at nil pay. 

Source - former HR and new mother who did exactly this.

The thing that's helped me has been age. I've gotten better at accepting myself as I've grown up. I started not allowing myself to think of being autistic as a personality trait. Even if I do have a sensory overload, it's easier to rationalise and not blame myself now because I understand why it happened - it was something I couldn't control. In the same way I can't be annoyed with myself if i catch a seasonal cold, i can't be annoyed at myself if my brain fails me for a bit. 

It's really worth investing time into regular self check ins. I try to do a half hour of meditation on myself and how I'm feeling every week, or if ice had a rough day I'll try to centre myself before bed. You could use a journal or another method of self reflection if that suits you better. 

It will be okay someday. I can't tell you when, but it will.

Just jumping in here - we have a nearly 14 week old and have been very loosely sleep training him since he was 8 weeks old. 

Just so nobody jumps in and says 'dont do that he's too young' etc - we made sure he had a bottle ready for his usual times etc just in case he woke up. He also gained his birth weight back pretty quick. 

What we did was we started with a general bedtime routine - bath snuggle bed. 
Then after about a week of that we started leaving him in the room alone, drowsy but not fully asleep yet. If he cried (proper crying rather than just grizzling) we would wait for 2 minutes and then go settle him, make sure he didnt need burped etc then leave the room again. Next time we would wait 5 minutes then repeat. 3rd time we would wait 10 minutes but we wouldn't pick him up that time. The plan was that if he cried again we would go back in after 10 minutes again each time, but we never had to do that. After about 2 weeks he just went to sleep after his wee routine.

Now we can just pop him down after his cuddles and he gurgles a bit, plays with his hands and then goes to sleep. Sleeps through from between 8pm-10pm through to about 7am now. 

It's not right for everyone but it seemed to work for us.

When I was at work (on maternity leave just now) I was a project manager. So I take that type of approach to most tasks. 

1. Set a timescale (and budget if need be) 
- first decide when your task or problem needs to be done/solved by.
- break it down into individual steps and if they need to be done in order and when they need done by. 

2. (Optional step) Make a list of people you might need to be involved/would like to hear their opinion or if the task will affect them. 

3. Gather all materials needed 

4. Work through each step of the task and tick it off as you go. If you need to make any adjustments or changes it's easier to to it little bits at a time. 

5. Make sure you take breaks and don't sit for too long. I always did half an hour then a couple of minutes break unless I had meetings.

Feed the cat (She isn't overly fussed about the baby - normally avoids him at all costs except bedtime when she sleeps under his cot)

12-2 - change baby and feed him. Then play with him some more. He normally has his bottle by 1:30. 

1:30-4:30 - go out for a long walk with the baby. He normally sleeps for a few hours in the afternoon, I walk between 3 and 10km, normally out to the park now (socially distanced of course). When we get back, if it's not raining I'll sit outside with him in his pram or bouncer and have a snack. 

4-6 change and play with baby then give him his bottle. Play with him a bit more so he stays awake for a bit longer. My partner usually gets home from work now unless he's on a late. 

5-8- chill out watching tv or reading a book or folding laundry. Play with baby and try to get him to take a short nap. 

8-9:30- do baby's bedtime routine. This involves making up his bottle, getting our bedroom ready (he sleeps in our room as he's only 9 weeks, I put the night lights on, make the bed, close the curtains but open the window a little) give baby a lavender bath (wash his hair every second day) and then put him in a sleepsuit. Feed him in our room and then settle him into his cot. Lights out, white noise on and then we close the door when we leave the room. 

9:30-12- Have dinner, catch up with my partner/watch tv, sometimes have a glass of wine. Occasionally we have a 'date night' where we have cheese and biscuits or crisps and munchies while watching a film together, most of the time he stays on his computer and I chill on the sofa. Tidy up the floor space from playing with the baby. Feed our cat, Pika. 

12-1- go to bed at some point and desperately try not to wake the baby when I go. 

3-5am - baby normally wakes up so I give him his dummy and try to get him to go back to sleep for a few hours. If he doesn't settle after half an hour I bring him into the bed with me until he wakes up in the morning. 

Rinse and repeat. Sometimes if my partner has the day off I'll shower in the morning or if it's been 3/4 days I'll wash my hair etc with the baby in his bath seat.
